learningObjectives: Explain how the Search duplicate Cases logic identifies potential duplicates using basic and weighted conditions.
Configure a Search duplicate Cases Step and describe how users resolve identified duplicates.

elements.description: Automation Step for checking whether existing Cases resemble the current submission. Place it at the point in the Process where duplicate review is needed; a match is a candidate for review, not proof that two requests are identical.

elements.text: Think of a reservation desk checking a second booking request. First it filters out unrelated reservations, then scores the useful similarities. A staff member examines the candidates and either rejects the duplicate submission or continues processing a distinct request. Finding a similar reservation does not combine the two records.

elements.description: Each configured basic condition must evaluate to true before an existing Case reaches the scoring stage. An equality comparison can require identical dates of birth, for example. A failed basic condition excludes that candidate; extra weighted matches cannot rescue it.

A true weighted condition contributes its assigned weight (1–100). After the basic filter passes, add the matching weights and compare the total with the configured threshold. Equality with the threshold qualifies; the score is not a probability or a promise of display order.

The review lets the user confirm a duplicate (Resolved-Duplicate, ending current processing) or ignore the suggestions and continue. Opening the original Case to update it requires customized behavior; detection alone does not merge records or transfer their data.

elements.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 190" role="img" font-family="inherit"><title>Duplicate review at the configured Step</title><rect x="10" y="10" width="740" height="170" rx="12" fill="var(--pa-surface)" stroke="var(--pa-brand)"/><text x="30" y="42" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="var(--pa-brand)">Filter → score → review</text><g font-size="14" fill="var(--pa-ink-2)"><text x="30" y="78">All basic tests pass → sum weights of true conditions.</text><text x="30" y="110">Total ≥ threshold → candidates for review; no candidates → next Step.</text><text x="30" y="142">Confirm → resolve current Case; ignore → continue processing.</text></g></svg>
elements.caption: The configured Step filters and scores candidates, then supports a user decision. It is not an automatic merge.

examPitfalls.title: A failed basic condition excludes a candidate
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Do not let a large weighted total override a failed basic test.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Check that every configured basic test is true before adding weighted values.

examPitfalls.title: The threshold includes equality
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A score equal to the threshold is sometimes incorrectly rejected.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: A total of 50 qualifies at threshold 50 if the basic filter passed. Not every weighted condition has to be true.

examPitfalls.title: Confirming a duplicate ends current processing
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Do not substitute an invented Closed-Duplicate status or deletion for duplicate resolution.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The confirmed current Case uses Resolved-Duplicate; ignoring the suggestions continues processing.

examPitfalls.title: Search runs at the configured Step
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Do not assume every new Case is checked automatically at creation.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Add the Search duplicate Cases automation to the intended Process and reason about when the Case reaches it.

examPitfalls.title: Filtering is not a save-validation claim
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A description of the search algorithm does not establish every Rule form constraint.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Explain basic filtering followed by weighted scoring without inventing a requirement that the configuration cannot be saved.

examPitfalls.title: A candidate needs a user decision
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A high score is not permission to combine records automatically.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Review the records; confirm a duplicate or continue a distinct submission. Customizing original-Case updates is separate.

examPitfalls.title: A candidate list is not a ranking guarantee
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Numeric scores do not prove that the view sorts candidates or shows a statistical likelihood.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Explain qualification and review without promising display order, automatic best-match selection or data transfer.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A health care application receives the same insurance authorization request twice — once online and once by fax. What Pega feature helps prevent processing both as separate Cases?

options.text: The 'Search duplicate cases' Automation Step, which identifies potential duplicates using basic and weighted conditions
A When Condition on the Create Stage that blocks Case creation if matching data is detected
A Decision table that routes duplicate submissions to an Alternate Stage
A Declare Expression that automatically merges Cases with identical field values

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish required filtering, weighted qualification and the user decision.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The supplied automation supports review of repeated submissions; the request still needs an operator decision.

optionExplanations.A: The supplied automation supports review of repeated submissions; the request still needs an operator decision.
optionExplanations.B: A Boolean condition alone is not the candidate search and resolution experience asked for here.
optionExplanations.C: Routing logic can choose a path, but does not supply this duplicate-review automation.
optionExplanations.D: A calculated property is not a mechanism for automatically combining submitted records.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A basic condition requires equal patient dates of birth. All other fields match, but an existing Case has a different date of birth. Is it a duplicate candidate?

options.text: No — the date-of-birth basic test fails, excluding this candidate before scoring
Yes — the weighted conditions still score highly enough to flag the Case as a likely duplicate
Yes — basic conditions are advisory; the system still presents the Case if weighted scores are sufficient
No — but the Case is put in a 'Possible duplicate' queue for manual review

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish required filtering, weighted qualification and the user decision.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Different birth dates fail the equality test explicitly configured in this scenario.

optionExplanations.A: Different birth dates fail the equality test explicitly configured in this scenario.
optionExplanations.B: Scoring applies after basic filtering; other matching fields cannot restore this excluded candidate.
optionExplanations.C: The required filter is not merely a suggestion that a weighted total can override.
optionExplanations.D: The documented failed-filter outcome is continuing the Process, not a special review queue.

practiceQuiz.scenario: All basic conditions pass. Three weighted conditions have weights 30, 40 and 30; an existing Case matches the first two, totaling 70. Does it qualify for review?

options.text: It depends on the configured threshold score — if 70 meets or exceeds the threshold, it is presented
No — all weighted conditions must match for a Case to be flagged
Yes — any positive weighted score is sufficient to flag a Case
No — weighted conditions require a perfect 100 score to flag a duplicate

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish required filtering, weighted qualification and the user decision.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The qualifying boundary is inclusive: a threshold of 70 accepts 70, while a threshold of 71 rejects it.

optionExplanations.A: The qualifying boundary is inclusive: a threshold of 70 accepts 70, while a threshold of 71 rejects it.
optionExplanations.B: One unmatched weighted comparison is acceptable when the remaining total reaches the threshold.
optionExplanations.C: A positive score below the configured cutoff is insufficient.
optionExplanations.D: The example does not impose a universal perfect-score requirement.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A user reviews a potential duplicate presented by the Search duplicate cases Step and confirms the current Case IS a duplicate. What action resolves it?

options.text: Confirm the current Case as a duplicate; it resolves with status 'Resolved-Duplicate'
Set the Case status to 'Closed-Duplicate'
Click 'Merge' in the duplicate Case panel to combine the two Cases
Delete the duplicate Case from Dev Studio

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish required filtering, weighted qualification and the user decision.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Confirmation resolves the current submission rather than merely noting a similarity.

optionExplanations.A: Confirmation resolves the current submission rather than merely noting a similarity.
optionExplanations.B: This substitutes a different status for the documented duplicate-resolution status.
optionExplanations.C: The described automation offers a resolution decision, not an automatic record-combination operation.
optionExplanations.D: Deleting a record is not the duplicate-resolution action being tested.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the role of a basic condition in the Search duplicate cases Step?

options.text: It filters candidates: a Case must satisfy every configured basic condition before weighted scoring
It contributes a fixed score that is added to the weighted condition total
It defines the Case Type to search — basic conditions specify which Case Type to compare against
It is a fallback condition used when no weighted conditions match

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish required filtering, weighted qualification and the user decision.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The filter tests must all pass; their operators define what satisfying them means.

optionExplanations.A: The filter tests must all pass; their operators define what satisfying them means.
optionExplanations.B: Adding points is the role of weighted comparisons, not the basic filter.
optionExplanations.C: This answer confuses filtering property values with a universal Case Type selector.
optionExplanations.D: Basic filtering comes before scoring rather than acting as a fallback after it.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the role of a weighted condition in the Search duplicate cases Step?

options.text: It adds its assigned numeric weight when true; qualifying totals must meet or exceed the threshold after basic filtering
It must match exactly — any failure eliminates the Case as a duplicate candidate
It defines the maximum number of duplicate results returned to the user
It is evaluated only when the basic conditions produce no results

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish required filtering, weighted qualification and the user decision.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A weight measures relative comparison importance; qualification still depends on the filter and cutoff.

optionExplanations.A: A weight measures relative comparison importance; qualification still depends on the filter and cutoff.
optionExplanations.B: A failed weighted comparison adds nothing, but other matching comparisons may still qualify.
optionExplanations.C: Comparison importance is distinct from limiting the number of results shown.
optionExplanations.D: Scoring requires candidates to survive the basic filter, rather than starting when none survive.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Does the Search duplicate cases automation automatically close or merge duplicate Cases when it finds a match?

options.text: No — a user reviews the candidates and may confirm the current Case as a duplicate or continue processing
Yes — Cases scoring above the threshold are automatically merged with the existing Case
Yes — the system automatically sets the status to 'Resolved-Duplicate' when the score exceeds 100
No — duplicate detection only logs a warning in the guardrails report

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish required filtering, weighted qualification and the user decision.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The operator decides whether the current submission repeats an existing request.

optionExplanations.A: The operator decides whether the current submission repeats an existing request.
optionExplanations.B: Finding a strong match does not combine the records automatically.
optionExplanations.C: No score, including one above 100, replaces the required review decision.
optionExplanations.D: The automation provides runtime candidate review, not only a design-time warning.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO statements correctly describe how basic and weighted conditions differ in duplicate search?

options.text: Every configured basic condition must evaluate to true for a candidate to reach scoring
True weighted conditions add their assigned values to a total compared with the threshold
A high weighted total overrides a failed basic condition
Weighted conditions must all match — partial matches are not counted

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish required filtering, weighted qualification and the user decision.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Every configured basic test gates entry into scoring. The comparison contributes its full weight when true; qualification uses the summed total.

optionExplanations.A: Every configured basic test gates entry into scoring.
optionExplanations.B: The comparison contributes its full weight when true; qualification uses the summed total.
optionExplanations.C: A failed gate excludes the candidate regardless of its possible score.
optionExplanations.D: Matching every weighted comparison is unnecessary if the threshold is already reached.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A duplicate search Step is configured with one basic condition ('Policy number' must match) and two weighted conditions ('Customer name' = 20 points, 'Incident date' = 30 points). An existing Case has the same policy number, same customer name, but a different incident date. Is it presented as a potential duplicate?

options.text: It depends on the threshold: the score is 20 and qualifies only if the threshold is 20 or lower
No — all conditions (basic and weighted) must match to flag a duplicate
Yes — the basic condition alone is sufficient to flag a duplicate regardless of weighted conditions
No — both weighted conditions must match for the Case to qualify

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish required filtering, weighted qualification and the user decision.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Only the name comparison contributes, totaling 20; the unknown threshold prevents an unconditional yes.

optionExplanations.A: Only the name comparison contributes, totaling 20; the unknown threshold prevents an unconditional yes.
optionExplanations.B: This incorrectly requires the incident-date comparison to match as well.
optionExplanations.C: Passing the policy-number filter does not bypass the weighted threshold.
optionExplanations.D: Both weighted comparisons need not match; 20 can qualify at a sufficiently low threshold.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Multiple potential duplicates are identified for a new Case. What does the user see?

options.text: A list of candidate Cases to review before confirming a duplicate or continuing the current Case
A single best-match duplicate automatically selected by the system
A warning banner only — no specific Cases are shown
The Cases are automatically merged into one without user confirmation

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish required filtering, weighted qualification and the user decision.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The review concerns whether the current request duplicates an existing record; list order is not guaranteed here.

optionExplanations.A: The review concerns whether the current request duplicates an existing record; list order is not guaranteed here.
optionExplanations.B: A selected best match would remove the review decision described in the topic.
optionExplanations.C: The candidate records are displayed for review, rather than an unspecified warning alone.
optionExplanations.D: Automatic combination is different from the documented confirmation or continuation choice.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA adds the 'Search duplicate cases' feature to a Case Type. Where in the Case lifecycle does this Step belong?

options.text: As an Automation Step within a Process in the Case Life Cycle
As a Stage-level configuration in the Stage properties panel
As a Case Type-level setting in the App Studio settings panel
As a When Rule attached to the Create Stage

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish required filtering, weighted qualification and the user decision.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Configure it as a Process Step; the check takes place when execution reaches that Step.

optionExplanations.A: Configure it as a Process Step; the check takes place when execution reaches that Step.
optionExplanations.B: Stage properties alone are not the specified automation Step.
optionExplanations.C: An application-wide setting is not the requested lifecycle placement.
optionExplanations.D: A When Rule does not itself supply the duplicate-search review Process.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What purpose do basic conditions serve before weighted scoring in a duplicate search?

options.text: They filter out Cases that fail the configured required tests before scoring the remaining candidates
They contribute numeric weights that are added to the scoring total
Basic conditions replace weighted conditions when the weighted score is zero
Basic conditions define the Case Type to search — without them, the Step searches all Case Types

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish required filtering, weighted qualification and the user decision.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Filtering eliminates unrelated candidates before their weighted comparisons are evaluated.

optionExplanations.A: Filtering eliminates unrelated candidates before their weighted comparisons are evaluated.
optionExplanations.B: This assigns the scoring responsibility to the wrong kind of condition.
optionExplanations.C: A zero weighted total does not turn the basic filter into a replacement score.
optionExplanations.D: Filtering conditions are not a guarantee of searching all Case Types when omitted.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Pega developer is reviewing how users interact with detected duplicates at runtime. Which TWO statements correctly describe the user resolution experience?

options.text: The user can review the candidates and confirm the current Case as a duplicate, ending its processing
The user can ignore the suggestions and continue the current Case when it is not a duplicate
Pega automatically merges the new Case into the duplicate and closes the new submission without any user decision
Duplicate resolution always transfers all data from the new Case into the existing matching Case automatically

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish required filtering, weighted qualification and the user decision.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Confirmation ends processing of the current duplicate; it does not require merging its contents. Ignoring the suggestions allows the distinct current request to proceed to the next Step.

optionExplanations.A: Confirmation ends processing of the current duplicate; it does not require merging its contents.
optionExplanations.B: Ignoring the suggestions allows the distinct current request to proceed to the next Step.
optionExplanations.C: This removes the user decision and invents an automatic merge.
optionExplanations.D: Data transfer is not inherent in duplicate resolution; original-record updates require customization.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO choices describe the documented condition-based design of duplicate search?

options.text: Use basic conditions as the candidate filter before evaluating weighted conditions
Assign relative weights to comparisons and choose the total-score threshold for candidate review
A threshold of zero guarantees that every flagged Case is a genuine duplicate
A matching Case-name prefix alone guarantees duplicate identity without field comparisons

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish required filtering, weighted qualification and the user decision.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Separate the required filter from the scoring comparisons so their different roles remain clear. Choose comparison importance and cutoff deliberately; this is configuration, not a guarantee of accuracy.

optionExplanations.A: Separate the required filter from the scoring comparisons so their different roles remain clear.
optionExplanations.B: Choose comparison importance and cutoff deliberately; this is configuration, not a guarantee of accuracy.
optionExplanations.C: A permissive cutoff is not evidence of identity and cannot bypass a failed basic filter.
optionExplanations.D: A name resemblance alone does not establish that two business requests are the same.

quickRecap.value: Checks occur when the Case reaches the configured automation Step.
Every configured basic test must be true; scoring cannot override a failure.
True conditions add their weights (1–100); compare the total with the cutoff.
A total equal to the threshold qualifies after basic filtering.
Continue to the next Process Step when filtering or scoring yields no candidates.
Confirm the current duplicate to resolve it, or ignore suggestions and continue.
Opening the original for updates is a separate customization; no automatic merge or transfer is promised.
